cases.description: The target section (0) has never been initialized, so `sections[0]` is null. The method should return false without throwing.
Section 1 is non‑null (a list was created by adding a different record), but it does not contain `recordB`. The method should evaluate the second operand to false and return false.
Section 2 contains `recordC` (added beforehand). Both conditions are true, so the method returns true.
Negative section index leads to an out‑of‑bounds array access; the method should throw `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
Section index larger than the internal `sections` array size (which is 4 for standard DNS messages) triggers an out‑of‑bounds exception.
A null record is passed. The list for section 3 exists (created by adding another record) but `contains(null)` returns false, so the method returns false.
Section 1 has been initialized to an empty list; `contains` returns false, so the method should return false.
The same record instance was added twice to section 2; the list contains the record, so the method should return true.
A record equal in content to one already stored (recordH1) is queried; although a different object, `contains` uses `equals`, so the method should return true.
